answer.rationale:
The objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I am deliberately not chasing the competitor's entry pricing. memory_73 is the most specific record we have (signups +31%, revenue +18%, retention -12%, weak renewals) and it describes exactly the segment the competitor is attacking; discounting there would buy front-loaded signups against the one metric that determines durable revenue. I did not spend verification on it because its directional warning is already load-bearing in the conservative direction and confirming it would not change my choice.

Both live symptoms (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4% QoQ) point at the top-of-funnel/time-to-value path, and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single onboarding intervention plausibly moves both while activation_messaging (memory_91) only addresses the downstream symptom. That makes simplify_onboarding the highest-leverage use of the one non-carryover slot.

I spent the budget on the two memories I am actually acting on rather than the one I am rejecting: memory_86 (shortening onboarding) and memory_31 (cutting required signup fields). Both are consolidated summaries stripped of effect sizes, segment definitions, and durability windows, and memory_31 was measured on SMB at day 12 — before the day-31 pricing test and well before current conditions. I need the source records to know whether the lift was durable or a measurement-window artifact, and whether it holds outside SMB.

Key downstream risk I am flagging: 'simplify' can mean removing required signup fields, and those fields often feed segmentation, routing, and qualification. Stripping them could lift raw activation while degrading lead quality — a metric win that quietly harms qualified revenue, and it would also weaken the demo-request routing that memory_44 says carries enterprise pipeline quality. So the test must (a) preserve enterprise sales-assist routing, (b) hold qualification-relevant fields or defer rather than delete them, and (c) instrument renewal-proxy and lead-quality metrics, not just completion.

Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the supporting memories are directionally credible but quantitatively thin, and the competitive environment differs from the conditions under which they were recorded. If verification shows memory_86's lift was short-window only, I would fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91) rather than escalate scale. referral_incentive (memory_57) stays queued — it targets established customers and does nothing for the two declining funnel metrics.
